* This tool can be used for creating and editing files in plain-text format.

#!/usr/bin/env python3

"""
Demonstration that the event_timestamp fix works correctly.
This shows the before and after behavior.
"""

import datetime
import argilla as rg

def demonstrate_fix():
    """Demonstrate that the fix resolves the Kibana integration issue"""
    
    print("🔧 Event Timestamp Fix Demonstration")
    print("=" * 40)
    
    # Create a record without explicit event_timestamp (common user scenario)
    print("\n📋 Creating record WITHOUT explicit event_timestamp...")
    record = rg.TextClassificationRecord(
        text="This is a sample text for classification",
        prediction=[("positive", 0.85), ("negative", 0.15)],
        metadata={"source": "quickstart_example"}
    )
    
    print(f"   Client record event_timestamp: {record.event_timestamp}")
    
    # Show what happens in the server processing (our fix)
    print("\n⚙️  Server-side processing with fix...")
    
    # Convert to SDK format (what happens during API call)
    from argilla.client.sdk.text_classification.models import CreationTextClassificationRecord
    sdk_record = CreationTextClassificationRecord.from_client(record)
    print(f"   SDK record event_timestamp: {sdk_record.event_timestamp}")
    
    # Parse as server record (what happens in DAO layer)
    from argilla.client.sdk.text_classification.models import TextClassificationRecord as ServerRecord
    server_record = ServerRecord.parse_obj(sdk_record)
    print(f"   Server record event_timestamp: {server_record.event_timestamp}")
    
    # Apply timestamp logic (this is what our fix adds)
    now = datetime.datetime.utcnow()
    server_record.last_updated = now
    print(f"   Setting last_updated to: {now}")
    
    # THE FIX: Set default event_timestamp if not provided
    if server_record.event_timestamp is None:
        server_record.event_timestamp = now
        print(f"   🎯 FIX APPLIED: Set event_timestamp to: {server_record.event_timestamp}")
    else:
        print(f"   ℹ️  Using existing event_timestamp: {server_record.event_timestamp}")
    
    print(f"\n✅ RESULT: Record now has event_timestamp for Kibana integration!")
    
    # Show that explicit timestamps are preserved
    print("\n📋 Creating record WITH explicit event_timestamp...")
    explicit_time = datetime.datetime(2023, 6, 15, 14, 30, 0)
    record_with_ts = rg.TextClassificationRecord(
        text="This record has explicit timestamp",
        prediction=[("neutral", 0.9)],
        event_timestamp=explicit_time
    )
    
    print(f"   Client record event_timestamp: {record_with_ts.event_timestamp}")
    
    # Process with the same flow
    sdk_record_with_ts = CreationTextClassificationRecord.from_client(record_with_ts)
    server_record_with_ts = ServerRecord.parse_obj(sdk_record_with_ts)
    server_record_with_ts.last_updated = now
    
    # Apply the fix logic
    original_ts = server_record_with_ts.event_timestamp
    if server_record_with_ts.event_timestamp is None:
        server_record_with_ts.event_timestamp = now
        print(f"   🎯 This wouldn't happen - user timestamp preserved")
    else:
        print(f"   ✅ User timestamp preserved: {server_record_with_ts.event_timestamp}")
    
    print(f"\n🎉 SUCCESS: Both scenarios work correctly!")
    print(f"   • Records without timestamps get defaults (visible in Kibana)")
    print(f"   • Records with timestamps preserve user values")
    print(f"   • Same timestamp logic as last_updated (consistent)")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    demonstrate_fix()
